_comment: EPISODE 3, TAKE A of three (seeds 4824, 4825, 4826). THE ONLY TAKE THAT ASKS THE QUESTION, and the take that DEFINES the episode: the mic, the street and the light in this clip are what takes B and C inherit, through a cropped still from this render passed as a second reference image (--scene-ref). Episode 2 proved a prompt clause cannot carry a prop between calls and a reference image can, so take A is generated FIRST, watched, and only then referenced. Five grammars on: pace, guards, mic, plain and the new `can`.

product.appearance: same white body, same dark blackletter lettering, same gold illustration
product.colour_ban: It never turns gold or yellow.
product._size_comment: The can drifted in scale in BOTH earlier episodes, because the only size words in the prompt were 'the same size and shape in every frame' -- a relation between frames, which a soda-sized can satisfies in all four shots. This is the absolute size, bound against the hand holding it because the hand is the only other object in frame at a known size. 19oz is a fact about this product, which is why the measurement is here and the grammar around it is in format_spec.CAN_SIZE.
product.size: a 19oz tallboy about two hand-widths tall, taller than that hand can span
product._state_comment: No `open_state` and no `opening_extra`. Both are the ungrammared wording and the can grammar REPLACES the whole state sentence: every can is CLOSED, SEALED AND UNOPENED with an intact ring pull. Leaving stale keys here would read as configuration that is doing something.

location._comment: NAMED CITY, which is new. Every episode-2 payload carried a London-SHAPED description with no city in it, and take C rendered New York off the same clause: a description satisfiable on two continents will be satisfied on two continents (SKILL.md Critical knowledge 26). Naming the city is the only prompt-side lever there is, and it is a help rather than a guarantee -- the guarantee is the scene reference, which is why this take is generated first.
location.description: a wide pavement on one street corner in London, outside a red brick building wrapped in green scaffolding, with a bus shelter to the left, parked cars along the kerb and bare plane trees behind
location.landmarks: The same scaffolding, bus shelter and parked cars

_question_comment: IDENTICAL BYTE FOR BYTE in all three episode-3 configs. Take A speaks it; takes B and C carry it only so ANSWERS_ONLY can quote the one line nobody says. Episode 1 gave each take its own wording and the viewer heard three different questions.
question: Quick question. What's in this can?
_props_comment: Plain and unprinted, both of them. No newspaper, no carrier bag, no hi-vis: a garment or a prop whose prior IS lettering beats the no-lettering clause, which is what episode 2's garbled hi-vis chest logo cost (Critical knowledge 24).
props: a canvas bag, a set of keys
_shots_comment: FOUR shots, two per person, which is exactly what PACE_BLOCK asks for ('each person gets TWO separate shots'). Episode 2's take A configured five and the fifth was a silent `react` beat that the pace grammar contradicts. Dropping it also buys the word budget the can grammar spends.

shots.subject: a man in his fifties in a plain navy coat
a woman in her thirties in a plain red jacket
